_what: The box's site-deploy STATUS payload and DURABLE RECORD payload — the key sets. THE ONE COPY.
_conformance: api/test/barkpark_web/controllers/site_deploy_status_payload_conformance_test.exs drives the REAL controller to a real 200 on both doors and asserts the EMITTED key sets equal the lists below. A hand-written fixture nobody asserts against is still a mirror.
_consumers: cloud/ reads this file through BarkparkCloud.BoxStatusPayloadFixture. cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/sites/box_status_payload_conformance_test.exs asserts BarkparkCloud.Sites.Deploy.normalize_report/1 still consumes every `status.consumed` key and that BarkparkCloud.Sites.BuildLog's @record_keys allowlist equals `record.emitted`. Do not retype these lists anywhere: the guard arm in that file fails on a hand-typed copy.
_adding_a_key: ONE LINE in the right list here, kept sorted, plus the producer and (for a record key) the control-plane allowlist. Nothing else in either suite carries these lists.

status._classification: Every key render_status/1 can emit appears in EXACTLY ONE of `consumed` and `producer_only`. consumed = BarkparkCloud.Sites.Deploy.normalize_report/1 reads it; producer_only = it is emitted and deliberately ignored by that consumer. `conditional` is the subset the producer OMITS rather than defaults when the value was never measured. `consumer_only` = keys normalize_report/1 tolerates that this producer never sends (older boxes, the log/console fallbacks) — they are not part of the producer's key set and the api conformance test asserts they are ABSENT from it.
status._folded_why: `folded` is the subset of `consumed` the control plane READS but does not ECHO: `state` becomes an atom, `exit_code` only moves the verdict, `stages`/`log` feed the stage fold. A sentinel-equality assertion on them would be asserting the wrong thing, so each has its own named behavioural assertion in the cloud conformance test — and that test pins this list, so a key moved in here cannot quietly escape the sentinel arm.
status._conditional_why: health_exit_code is OMITTED, never defaulted, when no HEALTH stage reported — 0 is the SUCCESS code, so a default would certify a gate that never ran. route_status/route_detail take the opposite discipline (present-and-null) because the value a default would invent there is a string, and null reads as 'nobody measured this' on its face. So `conditional` holds exactly one key and the reason is per-key, not stylistic.

record._lock: STRICT EQUALITY, both directions: this list is render_build_record/1's key set AND BarkparkCloud.Sites.BuildLog's @record_keys allowlist. A key on one side only means the control-plane route silently DROPS a field the box now sends (which is what had already happened to route_status/route_detail when this lock was built), or renders one it never gets.
